faq: Is hiding a button enough for security?
No. Hidden buttons are only a convenience. We also check permission on the server for every request, so a blocked user gets nothing even if they find the web address.
Can I change roles later without a developer?
With the Premium package, yes, through an admin page. With the smaller packages, roles are set in code, and we leave notes showing how to add or edit one.
Do you need my users to log in again?
Usually no. Roles are read from your existing user records. If your sign-in system needs changes to carry roles, we explain it first and agree the work in writing.
Does this work with my existing login?
Yes, if your login already identifies users, such as Auth0, Firebase or your own system. If it does not, our sign-up and login service can be added first.
desc:
Role-based dashboard views and access control show each person only the screens, numbers and records that fit their job. Ecom Swift LLC sets up roles in your own app and enforces them on the server, so hidden data stays hidden.

## What are role-based views?

Role-based views are dashboards that change with the person looking at them. A manager sees team results, an agent sees their own queue, and a client sees only their own account. The menus, buttons and data differ because each user is assigned a role, and the role decides what is allowed.

The idea is called role-based access control. It protects private data and keeps screens simple for everyone.

## Why is hiding a button not enough for security?

Hiding a button only changes what the page shows. The data request behind it can still be sent by anyone who knows the address. If the server does not check the user's role on every request, a curious or careless user can reach records they should never see, simply by typing a web address.

Real protection therefore needs two layers. The screen hides what a role should not use, which keeps the interface tidy. The server also checks the role on every data request, which keeps the data safe. We build both, and we test each role to confirm that blocked pages stay blocked.

## How roles improve daily work

Fewer options means fewer mistakes. A support agent who sees only the actions that apply to them is less likely to change something by accident. A client who sees only their own figures does not wonder about other accounts. Staff onboarding gets quicker, because each person meets a screen built for their job instead of an overloaded one.

Roles also support growth. As a team expands, you can grant and remove access without redesigning the product, and a log of role changes shows who gave access to whom.

## What good role-based views include

- A clear set of roles agreed with you, such as admin, manager, agent and client.
- Menu items shown or hidden by role.
- Buttons and actions removed when a role cannot use them.
- Permission checks on every data request on the server.
- A home screen tailored to each role.
- A readable message when someone opens a page they cannot access.
- Data filtered by team, region or customer where needed.
- An admin page for assigning and changing roles.
- A log of role changes.
- A test list that runs through every role.

## How we build it

We start by listing what each role must do and must never see. We turn that into a simple table of roles and permissions, and you approve it before any code is written.

Then we add the role checks to your existing login, using the sign-in system your app already has, so users do not need a new account. We apply the rules to menus, screens and, importantly, to every data request on the server. The Basic package sets up two roles with different menus. Standard supports up to four roles with server checks and role-specific home screens. Premium adds custom permissions, an admin page for managing roles, filtering by team or region and a log of changes. We then log in as each role and try to reach what should be blocked.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give each role the least access it needs.
- Check permissions on the server for every request.
- Test by logging in as every role.
- Record every change to a user's role.
- Keep the role names simple and meaningful.

**Avoid:**
- Relying on hidden buttons for protection.
- Creating a new role for every individual.
- Sharing one login between several people.
- Leaving old staff accounts active.
- Putting permissions in code that only a developer can read.

## Who this is for

This service suits SaaS products with several types of user, agencies sharing dashboards with clients, and growing teams where support, sales and finance need different views. It also suits an app that began with a single admin login and now needs proper separation.

## What we need from you

Tell us who uses your app, what each group should see and do, and what they must not reach. Send a description of your current login system.

Add us as a developer or collaborator on your code repository, so the role checks can go into your own code. We never need your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until every role is tested.
